newsitem.title: USA: Corning profits rise despite loss from spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Corning profits rise despite loss from spin-off.

text.p: Corning Inc. Wednesday reported stronger fourth-quarter profits, as a $4.7 million loss from the spin-off of its health care services unit was more than offset by growth in most of its remaining businesses.

Net income rose to $86.6 million, or 38 cents a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $83.5 million, or 37 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues grew 16 percent to $999 million from $822.2 million.
For the full-year, Corning had profits of $175.6 million, or 76 cents a share, compared with losses of $50.8 million, or 23 cents a share, in 1995. Revenues rose to $3.65 billion from $3.26 billion.

The latest results include a loss of $4.7 million from discontinued operations, after Corning completed the spin-off of its Health Care Services segment to shareholders. The transaction created two independent companies, Covance Inc. and Quest Diagnostics Inc.

The 1995 results include a $348.0 million pretax loss for Corning's equity in Dow Corning Corp., its joint venture with Dow Chemical Co., which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection that May amid a deluge of claims that its silicone gel breast implants caused health problems.

"We're especially pleased with the performance of the optical fiber and optical cable businesses, where demand is strong due to fiber hungry global markets, and with the emergence of opto-electronic components as a strong contributor," said Corning Chairman and Chief Executive Roger Ackerman.
"We also enjoyed very strong performance in environmental products, both in terms of market penetration and manufacturing productivity," he said.
The technology company also said growth at Corning Costar resumed for products for pharmaceutical research, and demand jumped for high-purity fused silica glass for semiconductors.
Profits also shot up for consumer and glass laboratory products due to ongoing cost cutting programmes, it said.

However, Corning's television products businesses fared worse than the previous year as the company expanded operations and faced a temporary drop in market demand. Quanterra, its environmental services company, continues to struggle in a difficult industry, it said.
Corning's stock fell $1.75 to $34.125 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
